*Patent strengthens intellectual property protection for preparation of preliposomal Annamycin lyophilizate*


**HOUSTON, Nov. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Moleculin Biotech, Inc.** (Nasdaq: MBRX) (“Moleculin” or the “Company”) today announced the grant of an Australian patent covering the preparation of preliposomal Annamycin lyophilizate, strengthening the Company’s intellectual property protection for a key aspect of Annamycin’s formulation technology.


Australian Patent No. 2020303572 was granted to Moleculin and The Board of Regents of The University of Texas System. The patent titled, “ *Preparation of Preliposomal Annamycin Lyophilizate* ,” addresses the preparation of Annamycin’s formulation.


“Securing this patent in Australia represents another step in our efforts to build a strong international intellectual property position around Annamycin,” said Walter Klemp, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Moleculin. “Our formulation technology is an important component of Annamycin’s development, and protecting this technology across international markets supports our broader intellectual property strategy.”


**Expanding International Protection for Annamycin Formulation Technology**


The Australian patent is part of Moleculin’s broader global intellectual property portfolio covering complementary technologies associated with Annamycin, the Company’s investigational anthracycline.


The patent portfolio includes granted or allowed patents in the United States, Canada, China, Europe, India, Israel, Japan, Mexico, Singapore and Taiwan. The application has also been accepted in South Africa, where formal grant is pending, while applications remain pending in additional jurisdictions, including South Korea.


Moleculin’s global patent strategy also encompasses additional technology areas, including methods for reconstituting liposomal Annamycin and lung-targeted anticancer therapies using liposomal Annamycin. Together, these efforts reflect the Company’s focus on establishing intellectual property protection across multiple aspects of Annamycin’s development and in key international markets.


Annamycin is an investigational anthracycline designed to address limitations associated with conventional anthracyclines. The drug candidate is being evaluated in clinical development for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and other difficult-to-treat cancers.


**About Moleculin Biotech, Inc.**


Moleculin Biotech, Inc. is a Phase 3 clinical stage pharmaceutical company advancing a pipeline of therapeutic candidates addressing hard-to-treat tumors and viruses. The Company’s lead program, Annamycin (also known as naxtarubicin), has shown to be an efficacious and well tolerated anthracycline designed to avoid multidrug resistance mechanisms and to lack the cardiotoxicity common with currently prescribed anthracyclines. Annamycin is currently in development for the treatment of relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and soft tissue sarcoma (STS) lung metastases.


The Company is conducting the MIRACLE ( **M** olecul **i** n **R** /R AML **A** nnAraC **Cl** inical **E** valuation) Trial (MB-108), a pivotal, adaptive design, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2/3 trial evaluating Annamycin in combination with cytarabine (also referred to as “Ara-C”), together referred to as AnnAraC, for the treatment of relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia. Following a successful Phase 1B/2 study (MB-106), with input from the FDA, the Company believes it has substantially de-risked the development pathway toward a potential approval for Annamycin for the treatment of AML. This study remains subject to appropriate future filings with potential additional feedback from the FDA and their foreign equivalents.


Additionally, the Company is developing WP1066, an Immune/Transcription Modulator capable of inhibiting p-STAT3 and other oncogenic transcription factors while also stimulating a natural immune response, targeting brain tumors, pancreatic and other cancers. Moleculin also has in its pipeline a portfolio of antimetabolites, including WP1122 for the potential treatment of pathogenic viruses, as well as certain cancer indications.
